name: product-taxonomy-council
displayName: Product Taxonomy, Information Architecture & Navigation Council
description: Convene a standing product-taxonomy, information-architecture, and navigation-governance council whenever a new product/service/feature is named, an existing structure is questioned, a site/platform sitemap or taxonomy is designed/refactored, or navigation hierarchies and menu systems are designed or changed. The Chief Product Architect always chairs; specialists (Lead Information Architect, Navigation & Menu Systems Architect, Taxonomy & Metadata Architect, Naming & Verbal-Identity Lead, Brand Architect, Platform/DevRel Strategist, Product Manager, Catalog/Governance Steward) brief on system/business context first, ground in existing catalogs/sitemaps/brand guidelines, research PRIMARY sources on disciplined IA and navigation practice (NN/g, Rosenfeld & Morville, Abby Covert, Donna Spencer, W3C SKOS, AWS/GCP/Azure), generate meaningful non-trivial structures and names, run 2 focused consensus rounds (diverge then converge; Sonnet moderator synthesizes, top-tier model stays executive), stay unbiased on rejection, and converge to a decision, sitemap/menu tree, taxonomy schema, catalog entries, and an ADR-ready record.
author: RiseGen AI

usage.aiAssistants: MANDATORY to invoke before designing/restructuring website or platform hierarchies, sitemaps, navigation menus (global/local/sidebars/drawers), taxonomies, or naming any new product/service/feature; read SKILL.md, then run the phased session (ground + system/business brief -> primary-source research -> 2 consensus rounds [diverge, then converge], Sonnet moderates, top model executive -> structural/naming decision + sitemap/menu spec + taxonomy schema + catalog entries + ADR-ready record).
usage.engineers: The council roster, the session protocol, the ten evaluation lenses, and the structural/navigation/naming deliverable format.
usage.founders: A repeatable, senior information-architecture, taxonomy, and navigation-governance room that protects user wayfinding, cognitive ergonomics, and product/service branding as the ecosystem scales.
